recipes.name: Mom's Beef Shish Kabobs
ingredients_raw: 1.5 pounds lean beef, cut into 1-inch cubes
2 green bell peppers, cut into chunks
1 red bell pepper, cut into chunks
1 large onion, cut into large squares

steps.text: Whisk soy sauce, vegetable oil, lemon juice, garlic, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and black pepper together in a bowl; pour into a resealable plastic bag. Add beef cubes and squeeze out excess air; seal the bag. Marinate in the refrigerator 8 hours or overnight.
Add mushrooms to the bag; squeeze out excess air and reseal the bag. Marinate in the refrigerator another 8 hours.

Preheat an outdoor grill for high heat and lightly oil the grate. Remove beef and mushrooms from the marinade, shaking off any excess liquid. Pour the marinade into a small saucepan and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 10 minutes; set aside for basting.
Thread pieces of green bell pepper, beef, red bell pepper, mushroom, and onion onto metal skewers, repeating until all ingredients are skewered.

Cook the skewers on the preheated grill, turning frequently and brushing generously with the marinade you prepared for basting until nicely browned on all sides and beef is no longer pink in the center, about 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Mom's Beef Shish Kabobs
raw_recipe.description: Beef shish kabob skewers with bell peppers, mushrooms, and onion. They're basted with a soy and lemon marinade for a tasty meaty treat from the grill!

video.description: In this video, we'll show you how to prepare Mike's mom's beef and vegetable kabobs. This family recipe takes a few days to prepare, but most of it is hands-off time while the beef and mushrooms are marinating in the refrigerator for ultimate flavor. Then, skewer them up with bell peppers and onion and grill until nicely browned.

review.reviewBody: Simple and straightforward marinade for shish kabobs! I used olive oil vs. veg. along with low sodium soy sauce. For the mustard, I used dijon left out the salt and cut the pepper in half. I reserved some of the marinade for the veggies and marinated the meat all day in a ziploc bag. I skewered the veggies (adding some cherry tomatoes) and meat separate basing the veggies with the reserved marinade. Overall, very tasty!

This recipe was phenomenal. My husband and I used it for our stay at home, personal Covid-19 4th of July barbecue. The holiday wasn't what we're used to, but holy cow we at least ate like kings. I seriously made an account just to give this a rating. We used olive oil instead of vegetable oil, marinated the beef and mushrooms together (out of laziness), put the beef on separate skewers from the veg and let the kabobs come to room temperature before we put them on the grill (took less than twenty minutes- got this tip from the magazine bon appetite). We used a meat thermometer and cooked until 160 F. Sooo goood!!

Very good. Used tomatoes and zucchini too. Marinated the lamb in plain yogurt overnight and then marinated the lamb and mushrooms in the mix for 30 minutes while the grill heated. Put the marinate in a pan and simmered for a few minutes and used as sauce over the kabobs.

This is an all-star, save this recipe winner! Your grandkids will love it if my 4 grandsons are any measure! My 2 suggestions or additions: 1) add the salt last and taste test as additions are made, even giving some resting time between additions, as soy sauce brands can have differing sodium content,until you're confident with you're recipe. And 2) try teriyaki sauce for soy. Another omg thats so good version!( again, following #1). I think the basic underpinnings of this recipe have a lot of legs for other changes too, but its really hard to want to mess with a winner!
Made it for New Years. Used my vacu packer marinate bowl just an hour before grilling. Excellent. Will keep this recipe for future.

We LOVE the flavors in this recipe! Even marinating for 30 minutes provides lots of flavor! Some alterations we have made: We use chicken breast and sirloin steak, we add a little more garlic and a large splash of pineapple juice to the marinade. Instead of 2 bell peppers, we use 1 green bell pepper and a whole can of pineapple chunks (portion of juice for marinade). We skewer each type vegetable and protein separately on skewers to cook more evenly since our vegetables tended to cook faster than our proteins.

This recipe has great reviews for a reason. The whole family enjoyed it. Marinated the meat overnight. Used EVOO instead of veg. oil, lime juice instead of lemon, and for the mustard I used honey mustard I had from whataburger. My husband said the marinade was restaurant quality for sure. 5 STARS

We thought this was the best shish kebab recipe ever! The marinade was amazing! I really liked the idea of boiling down the marinade to make it stronger and brushing it over everything else on the skewer before barbecuing. It made it moist and flavorful. ??
Really great flavor with the marinade. I would not add salt next time, as the soy was salty. We also cooked the meat on one skewer and veggies on a different one because the cook times are different.
This one of my go to recipes. I do make the beef on one kabob and the veggies on another in order to get the cooking times appropriate.

I decided to decrease the amount of salt by almost 1/2, Most cooks know soy & worcestershire sauces are salty to begin with. I still felt I could have decreased the amount further. Next time, I'll go for 1/4 tspn. Thought lemon in this marinade was a strange ingredient, but was pleasantly surprised. Also pressed a large clove of garlic. In retrospect, 16 hours of total marinading time seems a bit excessive, will try adding the meat & mushrooms together for 8 hours total marinading. LOVED the mushrooms marinated this way, why couldn't I marinade ALL the veggies? Hmmmm? I will make again, will tweak to my personal tastes. I can see this being a good base for other meats & veggies.
Simple recipe with ingredients we already had! Great flavor and instructions. I’ll just use a little less salt next time as many of the ingredients are adding salt.

Delicious but remember to start marinating a couple days in advance. I add sweet cherry tomatoes (called “sugar bombs” at my grocery store) and fresh pineapple chunks to the skewers. Easy fun and so good. EVERYONE loves these.
Really great flavour, idk if its just the kind of soy sauce I buy but it definitely doesn't need additional salt. So great though. Makes a great stir fry too.

Delicious. Only thing I did differently was to add a couple grape tomatoes to each skewer. The mushrooms are SO good. I didn't have time to marinade for 16 hrs only about 8 but everything was awesome.
both children loved it. subbed: lime juice, garlic powder. only marinated 5 hours. amazing!
Great flavors. My family loved it.
This is a great flavor bomb! I just basted our kabobs a half-hour before grilling. I'm so happy I came across this marinade recipe! Thank you! I don't comment alot, so that means something! Kudos!!

I made them for July 4th. I made the marinade and sealed it in bags with the beef a day before. I’m not a mushroom fan, so I did not add them. On the 4th, I took it out of the fridge for 30 min before grilling. Everything was seasoned perfectly. I love using the cooked marinade to baste. Absolutely delicious!!!
I made this today and the family loved it. I grilled them on a big green and they were great!
